kind: bounded source-only standards and ownership audit

findings.problem: Failed emulator/snapshot refusal still force-stops the selected browser through unconditional entry cleanup before any owned launch action.
findings.caller_evidence: browser_launch.py400-407 stores session only after successful inner entry. test_android_device.py210-265 excludes clear/kill-all/start but not force-stop; healthy test323-327 states guards precede stops.
findings.limits: No pm-clear after refusal is established. No device was contacted.
findings.proposal: Tests first: exact physical and cold-boot refusal with only read-only getprop commands allowed; preserve the original refusal object if cleanup is adversarial. Register ownership only after guards pass and condition cleanup on acquired actions.

findings.problem: push_text pushes remote configuration then performs fallible chmod before the session records configured=True. A successful push followed by chmod failure leaves the acquired file outside cleanup ownership.
findings.caller_evidence: LaunchedBrowser.android_launch passes fixed browser configuration paths; _start owns the push; __exit__ removes only when configured.
findings.limits: Controlled post-push failure is a source path; an actual remote leftover has not been measured. Partial push/reverse completion on remote timeout remains a distinct hypothesis.
findings.proposal: Tests first: call the actual push_text/session flow with an exact post-push chmod fault and an independently retained remote-file witness/command recorder; target removal before backup. Record pending file ownership before the fallible phase after guards, with explicit treatment of pre-existing paths.

findings.problem: Timeout/OSError/interruption in one cleanup operation stops all later owned cleanup attempts. During failed entry it becomes the raised primary in place of the initiating error; __exit__ ignores body exception details when called directly.
findings.caller_evidence: LaunchedBrowser453-461 composes the body primary with the one escaping session cleanup error, so outer body-primary retention is already supported; it cannot recover unattempted cleanup or failed-entry primary classification.
findings.limits: check=False ignores nonzero adb status deliberately but does not suppress subprocess timeout/OSError. Original entry error may remain implicit context; it is not wholly erased. No permanent leak or universal cleanup bound claimed.
findings.proposal: Tests first: acquire known reverse/config ownership, inject one exact cleanup error at each concrete action, require every later action attempted and all raw causes retained before backup; exercise entry primary, body primary, no primary, and interruption without swallowing BaseException. Reuse existing launch failure composition rather than a new generic owner.

findings.problem: typing_attempts=0 or negative is accepted; _start clears/configures the browser then falls through successfully without calling _open, even for intent entry.
findings.caller_evidence: Production LaunchedBrowser390-398 does not override the default three attempts. Existing tests use zero sleeps/timeouts deliberately, but none override typing_attempts.
findings.limits: No existing CLI exposes attempts. This is a direct AndroidLaunch input-contract defect, not a demonstrated ordinary CLI failure.
findings.proposal: Validate at least one launch attempt before device actions; independent zero/negative constructor controls and positive one-attempt intent/typed controls. Keep existing supported zero settle/typing timeout values.

findings.problem: Android plans never take turns, so async enter_browser executes synchronous AndroidSession entry directly on its loop. Blocking adb commands and sleeps prevent that loop from serving or delivering cancellation; Android exit is synchronous too.
findings.caller_evidence: snapshot.py1084-1102 starts serving then awaits BrowserDriver with Android choices (grep87/1144) and intent launch plan1030-1066. Alt-Svc main allows only desktop chrome/edge; no Android CLI reachability is inferred there.
findings.limits: Source establishes blocking/cancellation deferral, not a measured deadlock, capture corruption, or timing bound. The reviewed threaded Firefox cancellation owner only protects the takes_turns branch.
findings.proposal: Small independent actual-launch readiness control: finite owned adb command held after real subprocess readiness while an independent loop callback/local serving request must progress; separate cancellation plus eventual acquired-resource cleanup/error observation. Use concrete existing launcher machinery, not a detached wrapper or unbounded join.

findings.problem: Independent input guards and the session stages (guard, destructive start, config, reverse, launch attempts) run together without paragraph boundaries; CLI required-browser guard and plan setup similarly run together.
findings.proposal: When remediating these functions, separate the independent validation/ownership/acquisition stages with blank lines only; preserve statements/order. No arbitrary module split is justified.

candidates.name: CLI hold input
candidates.assessment: argparse float accepts values without a finite/nonnegative policy before destructive launch. No new policy, native sleep behavior or input limit is assumed; zero hold may be useful.

candidates.name: CLI opt-in scope
candidates.assessment: --allow-cold-boot sets global environment even for --print-arguments and never restores it. Frozen Git search found no direct same-process main caller; ordinary standalone CLI exit limits impact. A repeated-main permission test would establish the intended boundary.

candidates.name: Debug/YAML preference strings
candidates.assessment: Renderer escapes quote/backslash only and leaves names unquoted. Actual browser/snapshot callers reviewed use fixed names and ordinary strings; malformed newline input or parser acceptance was not measured, and no reachable untrusted preference source was established.

candidates.name: Shell numeric normalization
candidates.assessment: Digit-only input is range-checked then used in shell arithmetic; extreme/leading-zero semantics are not verified against the actual shell/emulator parser. Do not infer an exploit or introduce a port policy without a control.

candidates.name: Transient remote acquisition
candidates.assessment: An adb command can theoretically time out after remote side effects but before local ownership recording. This is separate from the concrete post-success chmod gap; no device completion witness exists.

ruled_out_or_retained: AdbDevice uses host argument vector with subprocess.run, DEVNULL stdin, capture_output and per-command120s timeout; reviewed CPython run kills and observes its direct child on timeout/interruption. This is not a process-tree or end-to-end budget promise.
URL/chunk arguments are shlex-quoted; command file is shlex-joined. Remote adb shell implementation was not reviewed, so exact remote quoting parity is not approved.
start-capture.sh quotes emulator path, ramdisk, AVD and user argv, uses exec and clears six proxy variables; extra args are intentional caller authority, not proof of immutable snapshot/GPU flags.
Malformed UI XML returns absence for bounded retry; check=False is deliberately used for missing/transient UI and cleanup. Not every ignored adb return status is classified as a defect.

Module/property files contain concrete identity values and comments but no apparent secret. Property authenticity, snapshot persistence, renderer compatibility and measured boot time were not externally/device verified.

Android README source workflow and opt-in descriptions align with current source apart from the findings. Missing Next/persona opener is recorded as prose debt, not imposed as a docs-directory page rule on this out-of-docs setup page.

Other caller/library files are partial only; frozen grep lines are discovery, not whole-file credit.
